claim: "The hora is a well-known circle dance, traditionally in a fast triple metre, in which dancers link arms and step and hop in a repeating pattern around a circle." (paragraph n13)
problem: The Israeli hora is a duple-metre dance (2/4 or 4/4), not triple. GCSE OCR-specific revision resources for this exact AoS3 spec (musicgcse.co.uk, studyrocket.co.uk) state the mark scheme accepts 2/4 or 4/4 for Israeli music/hora. Triple metre (3/8) is a feature of the older, slower Ashkenazi klezmer 'horah' (a related but distinct dance), not the fast modern Israeli circle-dance hora that this GCSE topic covers. A student who learns 'hora = triple metre' will lose marks on a metre-identification question, which this lesson explicitly trains for.
correction: Change to duple metre: "The hora is a well-known circle dance, traditionally in a fast duple metre (2/4 or 4/4), in which dancers link arms and step and hop in a repeating pattern around a circle."

claim: Hora — "An Israeli circle dance, traditionally in a fast triple metre."
problem: Same error as the content_html paragraph: the Israeli hora is duple (2/4 or 4/4), not triple. This glossary entry restates and reinforces the wrong metre, and it is also used verbatim as a distractor option text in knowledge_checks[2] (the dabke MCQ), so the false 'triple metre' claim appears three times across this lesson.
correction: Change to: "An Israeli circle dance, traditionally in a fast duple metre (2/4 or 4/4)."

claim: "These are cylindrical, double-headed bass drums played with a stick, usually made in three sizes — the largest and lowest-pitched kenkeni, the middle-sized sangban, and the largest dundunba" (paragraph n7)
problem: This is backwards and self-contradictory (it calls both kenkeni AND dundunba 'the largest'). In the standard Mande dunun set, the dundunba is the largest and lowest-pitched, the sangban is middle, and the kenkeni is the smallest and highest-pitched — the exact opposite of what is stated here. This directly contradicts the lesson's own flashcard_questions entry ('What are the three dunun drums, from lowest to highest role?' → 'Dundunba, sangban and kenkeni'), which has the order correct. A student who learns the content_html version will misidentify dunun sizes/pitches in the exam.
correction: Change to: "...usually made in three sizes — the largest and lowest-pitched dundunba, the middle-sized sangban, and the smallest and highest-pitched kenkeni — each playing an interlocking part..."

claim: "...gamak (a rapid oscillation or shake around a note), and微 microtonal inflections to decorate the melodic line." (paragraph n8)
problem: A stray Chinese character (微, meaning 'micro/subtle') is embedded in the English sentence directly before 'microtonal', apparently a generation/encoding artifact. Not a factual error, but it is garbled text visible to students in the published lesson.
correction: Remove the stray character: "...gamak (a rapid oscillation or shake around a note), and subtle microtonal inflections to decorate the melodic line."
